chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): When I stand for prayer, I recite 'Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim' in the Opening of the Quran. He said: 'Yes.' I said: And when I recite the Opening of the Quran, I recite 'Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim' with the Surah. He said: 'Yes.'
He (peace be upon him) said: Do not recite in the obligatory prayer less than a Surah, nor more.

key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ: Basmala: The phrase 'In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful'

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting the Basmala and the length of Surah recitation in obligatory prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the permissibility of reciting the Basmala either independently or as part of the Surah, reflecting the scholarly discussion on whether it constitutes a distinct verse in Surah Al-Fatiha. It further establishes the jurisprudential boundary for obligatory prayer recitation, requiring a minimum of one complete Surah while prohibiting the recitation of more than one, thereby ensuring the structural integrity of the prayer unit.
